classification: selected post-hoc CPU FP64 diagnostic; the full nine-basis qualification remains unresolved
interpretation: The denser post-hoc scan found adjacent quarter-power pass points for 15 of the 16 previously unresolved row-directions. The remaining case is F[2,0], paper row/tet 172: its two sampled passing points are isolated (powers 30.75 and 31.75), with nearby non-passing values and nonmonotone error at the smallest deltas. This pattern is consistent with a cancellation/rounding-limited finite-difference regime but does not establish an absolute noise floor or prove the derivative gate. It remains unresolved.
limitations: Cases were selected because they lacked adjacent passes in run018; this targeted grid cannot promote the full nine-basis gate.
Branch transitions and failed endpoints are retained with status and reason.
No absolute numerical noise floor is claimed; repeated deterministic FP64 evaluation is not a measured floor.
